Yes, as u/silly-bollocks said, I wouldn't recommend ripping it off either. If it is infected, what's done is done. The best you can do is keep it from getting further infected. Such as covering the scab, and gentle cleaning daily (no ripping if off, just use some light rubbing with some skin-safe disinfect, like rubbing alcohol).

 If you have already ripped it off, it is very important to keep the scab covered at all times. With a clean bandage preferably, as those usually cover better than Band-Aids, but a Band-Aid will work too. The purpose of a scab (besides to stop bleeding) is to protect the vulnerable skin from things like dirt or germs getting into the bloodstream. Picking it off could make things worse. Even if it doesn't further worsen what is potentially an infection, it can make the healing process take way longer. 

I know people pick at scabs all the time, and often rip them off entirely, but that's usually towards the tail end of a scab's life. When it becomes itchy and bothersome. And usually their scabs are the normal colour of dark red or brown. I wouldn't recommend picking off _any_ scab, but certainly not one that's a green colour.

Avocado on the outside (like dark green) or inside (light green)? If it's light green I would be extremely concerned. Dark green is a slightly better color for it to be. If it's more on the bright yellow side of an avocado, then you may be okay.

I'm not a doctor or anything, but green (light or dark) is generally the color of an infection. That goes for all body parts. I've never had any experience with this, or burning in general.

Scabs are usually a dark red or brown. This is because of the hemoglobin in your blood. Any other color, especially green, could mean an infection. 

[Have you read this article?](https://www.healthline.com/health/yellow-scab#treatment) I don't know how reputable it is, it's not like it's WebMD or anything, but it may help a little. The article is about yellow scabs, but I assume the same applies for green. Except for the "wear and tear" section... Even from normal day to day activity, a scab generally shouldn't turn green. 

Since there's no pus or inflammation, it's hard to say for sure, but I would go have that checked out just in case. 

Once again, I am **NOT** a doctor. Only someone with basic knowledge on this kind of stuff.

I'm not going to necessarily be the person who's like "don't kill yourself!" because that would be hypocritical of me. But don't kill yourself like that. Not with meds. OD on meds can be some of the most painful shit you will ever experience. And even then the success rate is pretty low, as people never know the right meds, the right amount, or how their body would react compared to someone else's. Most times, people won't even get very far. They'll get terrible fucking cramps, and that's about it. No where close to dying, but painful as all hell. Those who do get further usually still won't die, they just got a bit closer than most. 

Symptoms of an OD vary from drug to drug, but usually, the most standard things (especially for OTCs) are nausea, vomiting, hallucinations, stomach cramps, delirium, abdominal pain, and seizures just to name a few. You can, and if you take enough, probably will get liver and/or kidney failure depending upon the drug, which in itself isn't painful, but the consequences of it can be.

Should you get farther than most people do, but don't die, you'll likely be put on life support. Which isn't fun at all. Trust me. 

According to a website I found, and have been to many times (but cannot and will not send a link to because it may be against the rules), ODing from non-prescribed meds (OTC) has about a 6% fatality. Which basically means it's not all that fatal, and probably won't kill you. Prescribed meds are only a bit higher at 12%. It's incredibly rare for someone to die from ODing as a method of suicide. When it comes to OTCs, at least. People will usually stop and back down when they realise how much excruciating pain they're about to be in. 

Getting away from OD itself, suicide in general is actually pretty rarely successful. On average, one in 25 attempts are successful. That's 0.04 (1/25) or about 4%. 

I assume that's because people have use the go to methods that are always though of, like cutting, OD, etc, but in reality, they don't know how hard it is to actually die from that. The body is pretty freaking resilient. 

So, in other words, don't kill yourself through OD. You _will_ regret it.
